A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSA research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-training experiments, commonsense benchmark scores, perplexity, long-context retrieval results, and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional continued-training experiments, efficiency measurements, and diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects alignment-loss accumulation: v1 overwrites the accumulated loss inside the layer loop, whereas v2 adds each layer's contribution. This is a limited correction to the stated algorithm; both versions otherwise specify the same equal-probability full/sparse routing and bidirectional SmoothL1 alignment. It does not establish that the training implementation changed.

E1.justification: V2 adds DCLM data for continued pretraining and efficiency testing at 64K and 128K contexts. SmolLM pretraining and the existing commonsense, WikiText, PG19, RULER NIAH, and LongBench evaluation coverage are retained. The expansion primarily extends the existing language-modeling scope.

E2.justification: The headline comparators remain FullAttn, MoBA, and NSA. Comparator membership changes in the NSA-component analysis: v1 Figure 5 includes selection-plus-window, window-only, and selection-only/MoBA controls that are absent from v2 Table A8's comparison with SSA. V2's NSA-nowindow corresponds to the earlier compression-plus-selection variant, rather than introducing an entirely new baseline.

E3.justification: Long-context evaluation is substantially redesigned around factor-4 RoPE scaling and an additional 10B tokens of continued training at 32K. ARC-Challenge changes from a stated 25-shot setting to 5-shot. NSA's window is reported as 128 tokens for both receptive fields, replacing v1's description of an additional half-receptive-field window. Figure 1 also replaces the 300M-model preliminary experiment with 1B-model results.

E4.justification: The core receptive-field, routing-ratio, alignment-direction, and alpha ablations are retained across v2 Tables 2 and A14. V2 adds L2 alignment, NSA-to-full-attention replacement tests, and RoPE/local-distance diagnostics, and revises the NSA window analysis. It removes the gated-attention comparison, fixed-budget block-configuration comparison, and long-context stream/alignment controls, substantially changing the supplementary evidence.

E5.justification: V1 does not state a repeated-evaluation or uncertainty-reporting procedure. V2 introduces five-seed commonsense averages with plus/minus quantities, lists the seeds, identifies LongBench and NIAH as single-run evaluations, and averages inference timing over 30 runs. These are evaluation repeats, not evidence of five independently trained models; the meaning of the plus/minus statistic is not explicitly defined.

E6.justification: Numerous results change, including SSA's full-inference WikiText perplexity from 15.19 to 15.28 in Table 1. Long-context tables are replaced and expanded under RoPE scaling and continued training; Figure 4 also changes the reported unscaled SSA trend from stability through 32K to divergence beyond the training window. Timing, NSA-conversion, and L2 results are added, while the core 300M ablation values remain. Changed protocols prevent interpreting the revision as uniform same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 adds Propositions 4.1 and 4.2, a formal capability/attention-gap decomposition, and Theorem 1 bounding attention-output error by dropped attention mass, with proofs in Appendices A and B. These go substantially beyond v1's formulas and empirical motivation. The sparse-attention complexity expression also changes from O((ks)^2) to O(Nks); the attention-sparsity definition itself is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction recast the problem around separate attention and capability gaps and introduce the proved approximation bound as a principal contribution. V1's abstract claim that sparse training improves extrapolation by mitigating attention sinks is removed in favor of broader long-context capability claims. Claims about strong benchmark performance and flexible inference budgets remain.

C2.justification: V1 attributes long-context failure to attention sinks; v2 Appendix L explicitly distinguishes the observed anomaly from sinks and instead explains it through RoPE frequency aliasing and token locality. Section 7.4 adds qualifications concerning SSA's retrieval beyond its alignment-training range, MoBA's longer-distance retrieval, and FullAttn's recovery after continued training. Appendix E newly acknowledges the kernel's lack of KV caching.

D1.justification: V2 adds an SSA code-access link, detailed RoPE settings, benchmark sample counts, decoding instructions, PG19 sampling information, and measured training and inference costs. Existing architecture and gating details largely move into Appendix C without changing. The newly disclosed evaluation details substantially improve reproducibility documentation without establishing that every corresponding setting changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for the efficient-attention survey, FlashAttention-2, DCLM, and WikiText, while removing the Vaswani, CoDI, and DoPE references. The related-work taxonomy and positioning relative to MoBA, NSA, InfLLM-v2, and DSA remain largely intact. Numerous publication and bibliographic updates concern the same cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method motivation, and results discussion are extensively rewritten around the two-gap framework. V1's background/observations structure becomes separate preliminary, theoretical-framework, and SSA sections. Appendices are substantially reorganized, Algorithm 1 moves out of the main text, and the alpha ablation moves into supplementary material.

P2.justification: Table 1 incorporates uncertainty displays, the long-context table is redesigned into parallel RoPE and continued-training comparisons, and the ablation table is reshaped and split. Figures 1 and 3 are redrawn and relabeled, Figure 4 is substantially redesigned, and the earlier appendix attention plots are replaced by RoPE, QK-product, and positional-distance displays alongside new tables.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important weaknesses in v1's support and reproducibility through a proved attention-approximation bound, repeated evaluation, measured costs, and explicit RoPE/continued-training controls. These substantially strengthen assessment of the central claims despite the loss of useful gating and block-configuration ablations. Some overstatement remains: Table A2 claims less than 18% training overhead, although continued training takes 176 versus 136 GPU-hours for SSA and MoBA at receptive field 256.
